cultural.vision_reason: A handwoven narrow-strip cotton and tinsel textile with geometric supplementary-weft banding, hand-sewn selvedge to selvedge — strip-weaving of this kind is a well-documented craft of the Papel and related Guinea-Bissau peoples, consistent with the claim.

physical.title: textile
physical.summary: Textile: six cotton and tinsel (plastic) (?) narrow strip woven lengths hand sewn together selvedge to selvedge. The ground weave consists of plain woven dyed black warps and bleached white, dyed black and tinsel (plastic) wefts. At each end of the textile there are groups of stripes of various widths. White cotton and silver tinsel run across the full width of the textile under bands of supplementary weft decoration. There a three bands of supplementary weft decoration one at either end which creates a grid pattern. The central band (panel) of supplementary weft decoration consists of groups of warp stripes and chains of geometric shapes running in the warp direction. The textile is finished with unworked warps.
